Assistant A's code is fundamentally broken. It assumes the two arrays are the same length and only compares elements at the same index (`arr1[i] == arr2[i]`), which is not how finding common elements works. Furthermore, it references a variable `common_elems` that was never initialized, which would cause a `NameError`.

Assistant B provides a working implementation. While the prompt asks to avoid "extra data structures," it is impossible to return a list of common elements without using a list to store them. Assistant B correctly implements a nested loop to compare all elements. Although modifying a list while iterating over it (using `pop`) can be risky, the use of `break` immediately after the pop prevents index errors in the inner loop.

Assistant B is significantly better as it provides a functional program, whereas Assistant A provides code that will not run and does not solve the logic of the problem.
